newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Kersaf Investments up on strong yr figures.
newsitem.headline: Kersaf Investments up on strong yr figures.

text.p: Shares in South African entertainment to hotels group Kersaf Investments Ltd rose on Tuesday after the firm reported revenues for the year to June 30 up at 2.8 billion rand from 2.6 billion rand previously, dealers said.
By about 1005 GMT Kersaf was up 100 cents at 36.50 rand.
However, volumes traded on the stock were small at 119,350 rand. "I would imagine they are up on the back of the results. They had good results," one dealer at the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said.

Kersaf's earnings a share, before exceptional items, were up at 351.0 cents from 317.0 cents, while the dividend was at 192.0 cents versus 183.0 cents a year ago when the firm reported late on Monday.
Dealers said also hoisting interest on the share was the firm's moves to invest in new future growth opportunities.
Kersaf anticipates recieving 594 million rand for the sale of its stake in entertainment group Interleisure Ltd, busy unbundling.

"The group has significant cash resources at its disposal which is pleasing as it is the intention of the group to actively pursue new investment opportunities within the hotel, gaming and leisure industries both in Africa and internationally," Kersaf's chairman Buddy Hawton said.
